title: THE QUICK PEOPLE OF THE PULSAR
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: This expands the day from an elderly human expert to a genuinely formidable nonhuman intelligence whose advantage is speed rather than size or force. The conflict is reciprocal and legible: the station's ranging pulse is ordinary instrumentation to humans and an unbearable long event to the plasma minds. A successful protocol can save both the crew and the quick people while leaving the counterpart free to keep or lift its shield.

First complete draft for S2, written to the selector's checks. (1) One frozen conversion: tick 4 microseconds; ruler of one tick to one second of human thought, so 1 human second = 250,000 ticks; chirp 0.40 s = 100,000 ticks = 27.8 hours; cadence 2.00 s = 5.79 days; quiet 1.60 s = 4.63 days; the candidate's earlier 'million-fold' figure was dropped because it contradicted the four-microsecond grid. (2) The polite-pause interval comes from an observed number (the torus's 0.52 Hz ring mode, 1.92 s per circuit), with two readings of it kept alive: Voss's driven resonance and Illuminara's one-circuit-to-agree reading; the gate is predicted at two circuits, 3.84 s. (3) Control, a half-circuit quiet (1.0 s) and a long quiet (7.0 s) have different predicted shield behaviour under the two models. (4) The rival can win: same-sign replay with a smooth e-fold ramp. The tell is a reverse-and-complement of a fresh strontium-drawn code on the 4 microsecond grid. (5) The seam opens on the predicted clock by the quick people's own action; Maule keeps the evacuation order in his pocket (burn line eight days of reserve, Day Sixteen at the current rate; signs Day Fifteen or not). Hydrogen arithmetic: intake 34 percent falling 3 points a day, reserve 22 days at full draw. Known weaknesses I want the critic to test: the 'one tick = one second of thought' ruler is asserted rather than derived and the story only says it is discardable; the reverse-and-complement reply could be thought arbitrary; Voss concedes quickly; the negotiation scene (Tarkov, orbit tolerance) is brisk and may state more than it dramatizes; the 40-step tail and the returned pause are tender but may be too neat.

The draft already delivers the promised exhilaration: its clock arithmetic is coherent, the station has a credible evacuation decision, the sealed table gives the rival model real predictions, and the reverse-complement reply is a clean observable that transforms first contact into action. Beatriz, Voss, Maule and Tarkov all retain consequential agency, while the quick people choose the seventy-one-percent boundary. The revision should now make that boundary and the proposed future cadence into an unmistakably reciprocal agreement, strengthen Voss's surviving physical rival beyond a linear resonator, and show the resource arithmetic that lets Maule responsibly shred the evacuation order.

Revision of T01 answering the three ranked points of GPT's T02 review. Decisions: P1 ACCEPTED (counterpart-authored choice: Door A and Door B declared in advance, strontium counter orders the blocks, B refused and A accepted with a timing correction to the start of their circuit, failure branch kept: no door means evacuation stays live; ninety-day review becomes a re-offer of both doors). P2 ACCEPTED (Voss's pumped plasma mirror is the strongest active non-agentic rival; discriminator is lag under starved pump; ten fresh codes; result favours a clock without claiming a someone). P3 ACCEPTED (Maule's reserve arithmetic and reinstatement threshold in scene 5; order shredded only after Door A). Kept per the review's protect list: the single quarter-million-to-one ruler and all derived clocks, the sealed table, 3.84 s gate and reverse-and-complement reply, Beatriz's raw-data and random-code work, Maule's authority, Tarkov's cost, the 71 percent boundary, the refusal to ask for a hundred, the unread forty-step tail, the returned one-circuit pause, and the R10 dialogue format. Bundled changes: P1, P2 and P3 land together, so any quality difference cannot be attributed to one of them alone. Words added mostly in scene 5; scenes 1 to 3 are unchanged. Known risks I want tested next: scene 5 is now long and may carry too much procedure; the sixteen-day margin figure and the threshold are asserted in a single speech; the timing correction could read as arbitrary. The 0.7 s offset and the 1.92 s grid are the same ring period read two ways, which is deliberate and leaves Voss and Illuminara both partly right.

The revision is materially stronger and close to final. The counterparty now has decisive agency: it rejects the human-preferred cadence, accepts the cheaper cadence only at its own phase, and leaves an untranslated tail. Voss is indispensable because her pumped-mirror rival survives the first spectacular result and loses only against her own precommitted lag test. Maule's evacuation authority is also grounded in explicit thresholds. The remaining defect is not thematic but causal: the final resource state shown after the door test does not yet support the number on which Maule shreds the order.

Final after one peer review of T03 (GPT's T04, one bounded point, accepted). Only scene 5 changed; scenes 1 to 4 and the title, deck and shape are unchanged from T03. Protected unchanged: the single quarter-million-to-one ruler and its derived clocks, the sealed table, the 3.84 s gate and reverse-and-complement reply, Voss's pumped-mirror rival and lag test, the ten fresh codes, Maule's authority and reinstatement thresholds, Tarkov's cost, the refusal to ask for a hundred, the unread forty-step tail, the one-circuit pause, and the R10 dialogue format. Word count is the worker's own count including speaker labels (T03: 2492 by the critic's count; methods differ).

Illuminara turns an apparent resource siege into a falsifiable encounter, lets the quick people reject the cadence that benefits the station most, and earns a safe shared rhythm whose arithmetic, consent and human costs remain visible.
